=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt:1-6 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The core profile omits the clarify-respond worker wrapper while the default standalone clarify path delegates questions to that worker and suppresses the Telegram alert.
  WHY: Core-profile consumers have no installed issue-comment workflow to answer the questions, so they can remain unanswered until the 60-minute stall-ladder backstop fires.
- scripts/clarify_data_provision_guard.py:90-92 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Prefix-only section-header matching can treat prose beginning with a recognized section name as a header and prematurely stop parsing decisions.
  WHY: Subsequent lettered answers can be missed, leaving the answer map sparse so an unsafe RECOMMENDED option may be posted unchanged.
- tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py:178-185 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The unauthorized-request test can encounter BrokenPipeError while sending its body because the broker closes the Unix socket after reading request headers.
  WHY: The error occurs before the test can assert the expected 400 response; the reviewer identifies it as an unrelated timing flake that a rerun should clear.
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:111–127 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The broker rejects unauthorized requests and closes the connection before reading the request body, while the test sends a body before waiting for the response.
  WHY: The reported CI run reproduced BrokenPipeError during `connection.request`, causing the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job to fail.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “Standalone issues [should be] answered by the clarify-respond worker”; the PR description says `clarify.yml` delegates standalone questions to that worker by default.
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt contains exactly 6 entries (ai-clarify, ai-plan, ai-implement, ai-review, ai-issue-pr-status, ai-cancel-on-pr-close); `workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt` still lists only ai-clarify.yml, ai-plan.yml, ai-implement.yml, ai-review.yml, ai-issue-pr-status.yml, ai-cancel-on-pr-close.yml. ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml is not in the core profile (it is in standard and full). The PR sets STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED=true as the default, so clarify.yml's auto-decide step sets delegated=true and the Telegram step is suppressed — but no installed workflow consumes the question. No diff hunk touches workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt; no clarify.yml step checks for the wrapper's presence before setting delegated=true; the README row for STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED does not mention the core-profile prerequisite.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/clarify_data_provision_guard.py:92 | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: Prefix-only matching for recognized section names can mistake a prose line such as “EXECUTION PLANNING” for a section header.
  WHY: _parse_answers could stop reading decisions prematurely and return an empty dict, causing the data-provision guard to leave unsafe options unchanged.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:1350-1353 (standalone_auto_decide delegation block), workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt:1-6 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The default standalone clarify path delegates to the clarify-respond worker and suppresses the Telegram alert, but the core install profile does not include ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml.
  WHY: No installed workflow acts on the questions comment, leaving the issue without an answer or alert until the 60-minute stall-ladder auto-answer fires.
- Requirement: "The clarify-respond worker for standalone issues" — the PR description says standalone clarify-respond "answers the questions clarify.yml posted" and the changelog says standalone issues "get their clarification questions answered by the Claude clarify-respond worker." The core profile (workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt) is the supported minimal install, yet it does not carry the worker workflow. This was noted in the linked issue description as "Not covered: Plan-stage questions on standalone issues still wait for a human or the 60-minute stall-ladder auto-answer" — butgoing silent for all standalone questions, not only plan-stage ones, is not in the documented gap.
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt (add ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml), or clarify.yml standalone_auto_decide step (add a profile-aware or installed-workflow check), or agents.md core-profile documentation (document that STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED should be set to false in core-profile repos).
  Evidence of absence: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt contains exactly 6 entries (ai-clarify, ai-plan, ai-implement, ai-review, ai-issue-pr-status, ai-cancel-on-pr-close). No diff hunk adds ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml. No diff hunk in clarify.yml adds an installed-workflow guard before delegation. No diff hunk in README.md or agents.md documents the STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED=false requirement for core-profile consumers.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "clarify.yml hands the questions to orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml and skips the alert" (the new default path) — implies the worker workflow must be installed for the delegation to take effect. Standalone issues should be answered by the worker instead of waiting 60 minutes for the stall-ladder.
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt (wrapper list) and/or README.md "Quickstart" / "Variables" sections.
  Evidence of absence: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt still lists only ai-clarify.yml, ai-plan.yml, ai-implement.yml, ai-review.yml, ai-issue-pr-status.yml, ai-cancel-on-pr-close.yml. ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml is not in the core profile (it is in standard and full). The PR sets STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED=true as the default, so clarify.yml's auto-decide step sets delegated=true and the Telegram step is suppressed — but no installed workflow consumes the question. Core-profile consumers therefore see a 60-minute stall before any answer is posted, vs. the previous immediate RECOMMENDED-only answer. Neither the changelog nor the new STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED README row calls out the missing-wrapper case; the row says "falling back to the RECOMMENDED options" without distinguishing immediate fallback (worker installed but failed) from the 60-minute stall-ladder backstop (wrapper missing).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/clarify_data_provision_guard.py: lines 90-91 (the new `header_token.startswith(...)` checks) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Prefix-only section matching without a terminator can treat prose beginning with a recognized section name as a header and stop decisions parsing.
  WHY: Subsequent lettered lines can be missed, leaving the unsafe RECOMMENDED option posted unchanged.
- tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py: test_broker_rejects_client_authorization at lines 178-185 (CI failure log_tail references lines 110-127 of the relay) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The unauthorized-request test can raise BrokenPipeError when the broker closes the Unix socket after reading request headers but before the client finishes sending the body.
  WHY: The test fails before asserting the expected 400; the reviewer says the flake is orthogonal to the PR and a rerun should clear it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- `Relay.do_POST`, lines 111–127 rejects unauthorized requests and closes the connection before reading the request body at line 131; `tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py:178–183` sends a body before waiting for the response. | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The unauthorized-request test failed with BrokenPipeError during `connection.request`, before it could assert the expected 400 response.
  WHY: The reported CI run reproduced this path: the broker rejected and closed the socket before the client finished sending its body. The `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job therefore failed.
- Requirement: “Standalone issues [should be] answered by the clarify-respond worker”; the PR description says `clarify.yml` delegates standalone questions to that worker by default.
  Expected change site: `workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt` and the default delegation in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`.
  Evidence of absence: The core profile lists six wrappers and omits `ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml`. Meanwhile, `clarify.yml` delegates when `STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED` defaults to `true` and suppresses the Telegram alert for delegated questions. A core-profile consumer therefore has no installed issue-comment wrapper to receive and answer those questions, and no clarification alert is sent.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
